skill.name: simpy
skill.description: Build and analyze process-based discrete-event simulations in Python with SimPy, including queues, shared resources, event coordination, monitoring, and CSV result export.
skill.summary: Model queues, resources, processes, and time-based events with practical SimPy templates and monitoring guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are lexical false positives: SimPy resource requests are not network calls, env means simulation environment, and Markdown backticks do not execute commands. The executable monitor performs an explicit CSV write to a caller-selected path, which can overwrite an existing writable file.

remediation.issue: CSV export can overwrite an arbitrary writable path supplied by the caller.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve exports inside an approved directory and require explicit confirmation before replacing an existing file.

content.value_statement: Complex queues and shared resources are difficult to evaluate before deployment. This skill guides SimPy models, monitoring, synchronization, and result analysis.
actual_capabilities: Creates SimPy process models with generator functions, timeouts, and scheduled events.
Models shared capacity using Resource, PriorityResource, PreemptiveResource, Container, Store, FilterStore, and PriorityStore.
Demonstrates process coordination through events, process completion, interrupts, and parallel waits.
Collects queue length, utilization, wait time, and event history through reusable monitors.
Provides a configurable customer-server simulation template with reproducible random inputs.
Exports resource monitoring events to CSV files for later analysis.
limitations: Requires Python and the SimPy package; optional plotting examples require matplotlib.
Provides templates and guidance, not verified domain-specific calibration or validation data.
CSV export can overwrite an existing writable file when given the same path.
Long simulations can consume substantial memory because monitors retain event histories.

use_cases.title: Plan Service Capacity
use_cases.description: Model arrivals, service times, staffing levels, queues, and wait-time targets before changing operations.

use_cases.title: Test Production Flow
use_cases.description: Simulate machines, buffers, priorities, failures, and throughput constraints across manufacturing scenarios.

use_cases.title: Teach Event Simulation
use_cases.description: Explain processes, resources, events, interrupts, and monitoring through focused Python examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic SimPy queue with [resources], [arrival pattern], and [service pattern]. Explain each process and report wait time and throughput.

prompt_templates.title: Add Priority and Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my SimPy model for [system] with priority resources, reproducible randomness, and utilization monitoring. State assumptions and identify validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Model Correctness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SimPy model for deadlocks, resource leaks, invalid event reuse, and biased metrics. Propose focused corrections and tests: [model details].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Capacity Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a capacity experiment for [system]. Compare [capacity options] across repeated seeded runs and summarize utilization, wait percentiles, throughput, and tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Simulate one server with random arrivals and service times for 100 time units.
Compare two and three machines for a production queue.
output_examples.output: Three machines reduce average waiting, but lower utilization may not justify the added capacity.

output_examples.input: Check a process that waits forever after an event reset.
output_examples.output: The event references are recreated independently, so sender and receiver wait on different events. Share the replacement event before the next cycle.

best_practices: Define entities, resources, processes, time units, and metrics before implementing the model.
Set random seeds and compare simple scenarios against analytical expectations before scaling experiments.
Use resource context managers and monitor data throughout each simulation run.
anti_patterns: Do not use blocking Python calls inside SimPy process functions.
Do not reuse an event after it has already been triggered.
Do not treat one random run as sufficient evidence for capacity decisions.

faq.question: What systems can this skill model?
faq.answer: It supports queues, manufacturing, logistics, healthcare flow, service operations, computer systems, and other discrete-event processes.

faq.question: Does it install SimPy?
faq.answer: No. Install Python and SimPy in your project environment before running generated models.

faq.question: Can it model real-time systems?
faq.answer: Yes. The references explain RealtimeEnvironment for simulations synchronized with wall-clock time.

faq.question: What metrics can it collect?
faq.answer: The included monitors track queue length, utilization, wait time, resource events, and container levels.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: Yes. ResourceMonitor exports event data to CSV, but callers should control paths and confirm overwrites.

faq.question: Does it validate simulation assumptions?
faq.answer: It suggests validation practices, but users must supply domain data and verify that model assumptions match the real system.
